(Un)Traceable Grain: Dirty Logistics

By: Harri Vithi | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Carte Blanche hunts down a logistics syndicate threatening the country's food security by the grain load.

Unique Selling Point:
Carte Blanche hunts down a logistics syndicate threatening the country's food security by the grain load.
- Intercepting a compromised grain load before it's handed over to a criminal syndicate
- Selling a sacrifical load to a legitimate grain leader: no questions asked
- Confronting criminals as they alter horses and trailers at shady yards
- Following the trail of a syndicate's grain hit

Summary:
The clock is ticking for the agricultural industry - criminals are engaged in a dirty game forcing farmers and transporters to play but there are no rules.
For years, the logistics industry had been under siege, no commodity is off limits for these greedy syndicates determined to profit off legitimate businesses sweat.
Ben Wepener is a transporter and a former cop based in Delmas. In the dead of a night in June 2023, he received a call - his truck stood stationary kilometers from the silo where a client's grain was supposed to be loaded AND, his Zimbabwean driver was nowhere to be found.

This set the wheels in motion for a one man investigation conducted by Ben. The goal: to track down his client's missing load.
Through his determined sleuthing, he tracked the grain to AFGRI's silos.
AFGRI is one of the leaders in the grain and production cycle.
How did his client's legitimate load, "hijacked" by a criminal syndicate end up in AFGRI's legitimate silos?

Further information:
How do we start the story:-
Option 1:
Ben on the stretch of road in Delmas
Ben: This is where I found my truck, with no grain - completely empty and abandoned"
Presenter: Where was the driver?
Ben: I have no idea just like the grain he was nowhere to be found.
Presenter: What did you do?
Ben: I didnt waste time, I started investigating

VO: And what he discovered will blow your mind.
FADE TO BLACK

Option 2: Open with track team chasing a truck or with presenter confronting criminals altering a horse at a trailer yard
VO: You're about to join us on a ride through the murky underworld of dirty logistics.

Elements Explored:
AFGRI
I am in the process of securing a Folio number from AFGRI which will permit us to sell a load at
a SILO. I will record all interactions with the buyer. The purpose is to demonstrate the ease with
which grain can be sold to AFGRI with few questions asked. Clearly, I have no agricultural
background - where did I get the grain?
Transporter, Ben Wepener has made arrangements with a farmer to provide a sacrificial load
which we can sell to AFGRI.
We will place GoPro’s on the truck as it makes its journey and a hidden camera on the driver to
record interactions once he arrives at the depot. The cameraman will follow at a safe distance in
order to secure a wide angle.
The process of selling grain to AFGRI will be recorded so we will be clear on the checks and
balances they have in place for interview.
Note: consult legal on the receipt of funds into my bank account from AFGRI.

Hijack or Handover
Within the scope of their operations they say 90% of so-called hijackings are pre-arranged
handovers between the syndicate and the truck drivers.
They say almost all the drivers implicated are Zimbabwean in for a quick buck to send home and
able to disappear because often they are not legally in the country.
The team intercepted a truck “hijack”a few weeks ago and seized the drivers property including
a phone. They have endless voicenotes and messages intricately planning the handover of the
truck and the load.
How we can use this:
As part of the interview with Chris, he can allude to this incident and playback a few seconds of
key moments of the planning between the driver and the syndicate to highlight the fact that the
transport industry is at the mercy of these drivers - especially if they do not conduct proper
checks.

Intercepted Truck Takedown
The source says hundreds of “hijackings” place on a daily basis. In fact, as I was sitting with them, they
showed me a truck they were tracking on their phones.
The calls come in unexpectedly as they don’t always have informers who know when robberies
are planned.
They’ve asked the team to be ready to receive a call at any time - even 2 a.m - which is quite
challenging from a coordination perspective. Especially since the camera crew and the
presenter would have to be on standby.
This requires some planning.

Cloning of trucks
The syndicate secures transporters trailer registration numbers and clones them to avoid
traceability. They showed me an image of a client’s trailer and the syndicate's
cloned trailer with the client’s number plates. To legitimize their clandestine operations, the
syndicate uses the cloned trucks to offload grain at the silos.
Not only do they clone truck registrations, they hijack horse and trailers which they completely
alter at shady trailer yards well-known to the team. Although they can alter license
plates, the VIN number is often what the team uses to establish the vehicle has been cloned or
stolen and altered. By altered, they spray paint, weld and use blowtorches in order to make the
stolen vehicle almost untraceable. These vehicles are then taken crossborder where there’s
allegedly great demand.
How we can use this visually:
The team will arrange a stakeout of a trailer yard and see what we can film from a distance.
After 1 or 2 days of surveillance there will be a takedown. They asked if we have bulletproof
vests - I said no and indicated we don't want to be in the middle of a shootout. They rather wear
GoPros in case such an action movie takes place. We will move in once things have cooled
down.

Extra Budget Items:
2x Research days
Cameraman for one research day to secure additional viz
Car hire
Camera hire
Binocular hire
Bullet proof vests

Press Release:


Gone Grain


For years, the logistics industry has been under siege: no commodity is off limits for greedy criminal syndicates determined to profit off the sweat of legitimate businesses. Now, they’ve set their sights on a valuable food source: grain. Criminals intercept truckloads of grain on their way to silos, then masquerade as legitimate traders to sell the stolen goods to the very storage companies it was destined for...and pocket the proceeds. It’s a scam that’s costing farmers millions and they’re almost powerless to stop the criminals. Carte Blanche tracks down one syndicate engaging in this dirty game.

Producer: Harri Vithi | Presenter: Govan Whittles

Script:


(Informer (Subtitles) Hello?

(Govan) Delmas: a key contributor to South Africa’s R100 billion grain industry.

(Driver (Subtitles) I’m a truck driver, actually. So I’m calling you for business.

(Khensani Masina Subtitles) For a business of what?

(Driver) Maize.

(Govan) It looks peaceful enough, but this is one of the country’s hijacking hotspots.

(Govan) It’s become the epicentre of a rising trend.

(Driver (Subtitles) I’m driving the truck that is loading 36 tonnes.

(Driver (Subtitles) The load right now I hide it somewhere myself.

(Govan) This is a recorded call between an informer and this woman: Khensani Masina. There’s been a warrant out for her arrest for almost a year.

(Khensani Masina (Subtitles) Oh you have another load which you are hiding?

(Driver Subtitles) I’m hiding already, yes.

Govan (Subtitles) What do they target? Coal and grain?

(Ben Wepener (Subtitles) At this stage a lot of grain and some of the other trucks carrying goods. There are a lot of grain hijackings in Delmas.

(Govan) Hot on Masina’s heels is Ben Wepener. He’s a former police detective and private investigator, but for the last decade he’s worked as a transporter in Delmas, ferrying grain from farms to silos where it’s stored for sale.

(Govan) We’re travelling this route with him because just over a year and a half ago, one of his trucks allegedly became one of Masina's targets.

(Govan) He’s trying to track her down, and we’re riding along to see if he succeeds.

(Ben Wepener (Subtitles) It was the 23rd of June, 2023. And early that morning around 6 or 7 o'clock I logged onto the tracking device.

(Ben Wepener (Subtitles) And I saw that the truck was stationary at Devon silos.

(Govan) Ben’s truck was stationary for hours. When he couldn’t reach the driver, he sent his mechanic to check. The truck was empty.

(Govan (Subtitles) So the freight was stolen?

(Ben Wepener (Subtitles) White maize, yes. Completely gone.

(Govan) 36 tonnes of maize worth R166 000 had disappeared. Ben kicked into gear, determined to hunt down the thieves.

(Govan) This is where Ben first noticed that his truck carrying grain was being escorted by an unknown vehicle using the CCTV cameras at a spaza shop here in Devon.

(Govan) In the CCTV footage, a white Mercedes is followed a few seconds later by Ben’s truck. The two vehicles appear again on another camera down the road.

(Govan) The truck’s tracker shows it stopping in this field.

(Govan (Subtitles) So, Ben tell me what happened on this plot?

(Ben Wepener (Subtitles) My suspicion is that they used the local township people from Devon.

(Ben Wepener (Subtitles) To load the mealies, They used 20 litre paint buckets. Then they scooped it up.

(Govan) The location of the transfer was carefully chosen.

(Govan (Subtitles) And I see that the AFGRI Silo is just here.

(Govan (Subtitles) When you look at your truck on your tracker, you won’t see that it’s not at the silos.

(Ben Wepener(Subtitles) From where you loaded the truck it drove to where it should offload, so you're at ease now. You're calm.

(Govan) AFGRI SA is one of the leading grain storage companies in South Africa. Farmers and traders sell their grain to AFGRI, which stores it before selling it on.

(Govan) Ben believes the syndicate approaches drivers as they wait outside AFGRI SA’s silos, convincing them to hand over grain in exchange for money.

(Khensani Masina (Subtitles) A tonne I think they’re selling for R 4000 something. Then I have to pay for a truck for R 35 000. It depends where are you hiding it.

(Govan) Masina evidently knows the grain industry well. And that’s because she allegedly works closely within it.

(Govan) Because where would you sell 35 tonnes of maize? The very place it was destined for: a legitimate grain storage business… like AFGRI SA.

(Ben Wepener (Subtitles) According to my investigations, Masina has a folio [number] at AFGRI. And Masina is linked 100%.

(Govan) AFGRI SA uses folio accounts to do legitimate business with traders and farmers. So how does an alleged criminal like Masina get access?

(Govan) Well, the process is simple enough. Masina applies on AFGRI SA’s website for a folio number - essentially a customer number linked to a bank account.

(Govan) Every load of grain Masina delivers will be accompanied by a delivery note that includes the folio number. Payment is then made to the matching account.

(Ben Wepener Subtitles) Folio numbers are willy-nilly allocated to people. Some of the people are not farmers at all.

(Ben Wepener (Subtitles) And they use those folios to commit crimes and to make money.

(Govan (Subtitles) Look Ben, that's a very big accusation.

(Ben Wepener(Subtitles) It is, yes.

(Govan) It is a serious allegation. Wepener is saying AFGRI SA’s own system allows syndicates to sell stolen grain without verification.

(Govan) When his insurance claim was denied, Wepener demanded AFGRI SA compensate him - alleging it received stolen goods.

(Govan) We asked AFGRI SA for an interview. They declined but sent a statement saying there was no evidence for Ben’s claims.

(Govan) Frustrated, Ben set up a sting operation to catch Masina red-handed. And he agreed to let us tag along.

(Khensani Masina (Subtitles) Okay, where is that place so that I can come there?

(Driver (Subtitles) I must know the price first.

(Khensani Masina (Subtitles) White maize - I’m going to take it for R 60 000

(Driver (Subtitles) Okay, alright.

(Govan) So the truck is in place and the security is armed this is a really important time - the truck is going to be parked on the N12 that's where the deal is happening but we can't be too close to them because it will tip off the syndicate - we're close enough to swoop on them once they arrive and inspect the maize

(Govan) We wait for three hours and then…

(Driver (Subtitles): Hello

(Upsound Khensani Masina (Subtitles) Yes,I’m on my way.

(Driver (Subtitles) : Alright. Okay.

(Govan) And now it's just about getting there in time to stop her.

(Govan) Here they are. looks like there - she's running she's running into the veld! They're giving chase! Oh there she is!

(Govan) Security soon catches up, though, and we get a chance to ask Masina some questions.

(Govan) How long have you been selling grain?

(Govan) She pretends to be completely clueless about why we are here.

(Govan) We know who you are.

(Khensani Masina) Who am I?

(Govan) You're trying to buy grain that you thought was stolen

(Khensani Masina) No, I am not trying to buy anything. I was not trying to buy anything from anyone.

(Govan) You are Khensani Masina ?

(Khensani Masina) Yes I am Khensani

(Khensani Masina) I do have documents, can I show you my documents?

(Govan) Masina claims she leases a farm but doesn’t show us proof.

(Govan) Do you have a folio number at AFGRI SA?

(Khensani Masina) Yes, I do

(Govan) But her story about why she’s here gets a little confusing.

(Khensani Masina) This guy just called me and told me that he wants to see me

(Govan) No, he wanted to sell stolen grain

(Khensani Masina) NO, I didn't…

(Govan) And you said yes.

(Govan) We've got you recorded

(Khensani Masina) Yes, it’s fine

(Govan) We've got you recorded

(Khensani Masina) Recorded with what?

(Govan) Can you tell me why do you buy stolen grain

(Khensani Masina) If people call me they'll say come I have this ..I'm coming.

(Govan) So you don't check where the grain comes from?

(Khensani Masina) I do check.

(Govan) Are you running a grain theft syndicate Khensani?

(Khensani Masina) No sir,no.

(Govan) How long have you been selling grain to AFGRI SA?

(Khensani Masina) I've been selling grain I think for almost 4 years now.

(Govan) In other words, for the past 4 years Masina has probably been selling stolen grain to AFGRI SA.

(Govan) We asked for confirmation on whether Masina has a folio account. AFGRI SA declined, citing confidentiality laws

(Govan) AFGRI SA denied that it knowingly deals in stolen grain, or allocates accounts to criminals.

(Govan) But it did admit that it only began to conduct site visits to confirm that its clients are in fact farmers, in October last year.

(Khensani Masina) I don't know who are these guys and he's saying that this guy...yes.

(Govan) My name is Govan Whittles from Carte Blanche. This is a sting operation and you've just been caught.

(Khensani Masina) But I don't know the guy he just called me to come and see him.

(Govan) We've recorded all your communication with him. You're in a lot of trouble.

(Govan) The police are here and Ben's going to show them the warrant of arrest...Nkensani is smiling...she's clearly not afraid of them.

(Govan) What she is worried about is the phone she says she lost in the maize field.

(Govan) You're looking for a tilili...

(Khensani Masina) Yes, tilili.

(Govan) You know those phones are notorious for being used in crime, isn't that right officer?

(Govan) I don't know if you believe in irony?

(Khensani Masina) What is irony?

(Govan) It's ironic that you're being arrested for grain theft and you're walking through a mealie field.

(Khensani Masina) I do have the mealie field also.

(Govan) Here's your smaller phone. You must be so relieved!

(Govan) Ben, is this the woman that you suspect of stealing the load that you were transporting?

(Ben Wepener) That is 100% her. She confirmed here on the site that she does have a folio number with AFGRI.

(Govan) With Masina finally in custody and on her way to police cells, the truck driver covers the load up for safe delivery to its rightful owner.

(Govan) On Ben’s information, two alleged members of the syndicate have now been arrested. He’s back on the hunt for two more.

Press Release: Gone Grain For years, the logistics industry has been under siege: no commodity is off limits for greedy criminal syndicates determined to profit off the sweat of legitimate businesses. Now, they’ve set their sights on a valuable food source: grain. Criminals intercept truckloads of grain on their way to silos, then masquerade as legitimate traders to sell the stolen goods to the very storage companies it was destined for...and pocket the proceeds. It’s a scam that’s costing farmers millions and they’re almost powerless to stop the criminals. Carte Blanche tracks down one syndicate engaging in this dirty game. Producer: Harri Vithi | Presenter: Govan Whittles Script: (Informer (Subtitles) Hello? (Govan) Delmas: a key contributor to South Africa’s R100 billion grain industry. (Driver (Subtitles) I’m a truck driver, actually. So I’m calling you for business. (Khensani Masina Subtitles) For a business of what? (Driver) Maize. (Govan) It looks peaceful enough, but this is one of the country’s hijacking hotspots. (Govan) It’s become the epicentre of a rising trend. (Driver (Subtitles) I’m driving the truck that is loading 36 tonnes. (Driver (Subtitles) The load right now I hide it somewhere myself. (Govan) This is a recorded call between an informer and this woman: Khensani Masina. There’s been a warrant out for her arrest for almost a year. (Khensani Masina (Subtitles) Oh you have another load which you are hiding? (Driver Subtitles) I’m hiding already, yes. Govan (Subtitles) What do they target? Coal and grain? (Ben Wepener (Subtitles) At this stage a lot of grain and some of the other trucks carrying goods. There are a lot of grain hijackings in Delmas. (Govan) Hot on Masina’s heels is Ben Wepener. He’s a former police detective and private investigator, but for the last decade he’s worked as a transporter in Delmas, ferrying grain from farms to silos where it’s stored for sale. (Govan) We’re travelling this route with him because just over a year and a half ago, one of his trucks allegedly became one of Masina's targets. (Govan) He’s trying to track her down, and we’re riding along to see if he succeeds. (Ben Wepener (Subtitles) It was the 23rd of June, 2023. And early that morning around 6 or 7 o'clock I logged onto the tracking device. (Ben Wepener (Subtitles) And I saw that the truck was stationary at Devon silos. (Govan) Ben’s truck was stationary for hours. When he couldn’t reach the driver, he sent his mechanic to check. The truck was empty. (Govan (Subtitles) So the freight was stolen? (Ben Wepener (Subtitles) White maize, yes. Completely gone. (Govan) 36 tonnes of maize worth R166 000 had disappeared. Ben kicked into gear, determined to hunt down the thieves. (Govan) This is where Ben first noticed that his truck carrying grain was being escorted by an unknown vehicle using the CCTV cameras at a spaza shop here in Devon. (Govan) In the CCTV footage, a white Mercedes is followed a few seconds later by Ben’s truck. The two vehicles appear again on another camera down the road. (Govan) The truck’s tracker shows it stopping in this field. (Govan (Subtitles) So, Ben tell me what happened on this plot? (Ben Wepener (Subtitles) My suspicion is that they used the local township people from Devon. (Ben Wepener (Subtitles) To load the mealies, They used 20 litre paint buckets. Then they scooped it up. (Govan) The location of the transfer was carefully chosen. (Govan (Subtitles) And I see that the AFGRI Silo is just here. (Govan (Subtitles) When you look at your truck on your tracker, you won’t see that it’s not at the silos. (Ben Wepener(Subtitles) From where you loaded the truck it drove to where it should offload, so you're at ease now. You're calm. (Govan) AFGRI SA is one of the leading grain storage companies in South Africa. Farmers and traders sell their grain to AFGRI, which stores it before selling it on. (Govan) Ben believes the syndicate approaches drivers as they wait outside AFGRI SA’s silos, convincing them to hand over grain in exchange for money. (Khensani Masina (Subtitles) A tonne I think they’re selling for R 4000 something. Then I have to pay for a truck for R 35 000. It depends where are you hiding it. (Govan) Masina evidently knows the grain industry well. And that’s because she allegedly works closely within it. (Govan) Because where would you sell 35 tonnes of maize? The very place it was destined for: a legitimate grain storage business… like AFGRI SA. (Ben Wepener (Subtitles) According to my investigations, Masina has a folio [number] at AFGRI. And Masina is linked 100%. (Govan) AFGRI SA uses folio accounts to do legitimate business with traders and farmers. So how does an alleged criminal like Masina get access? (Govan) Well, the process is simple enough. Masina applies on AFGRI SA’s website for a folio number - essentially a customer number linked to a bank account. (Govan) Every load of grain Masina delivers will be accompanied by a delivery note that includes the folio number. Payment is then made to the matching account. (Ben Wepener Subtitles) Folio numbers are willy-nilly allocated to people. Some of the people are not farmers at all. (Ben Wepener (Subtitles) And they use those folios to commit crimes and to make money. (Govan (Subtitles) Look Ben, that's a very big accusation. (Ben Wepener(Subtitles) It is, yes. (Govan) It is a serious allegation. Wepener is saying AFGRI SA’s own system allows syndicates to sell stolen grain without verification. (Govan) When his insurance claim was denied, Wepener demanded AFGRI SA compensate him - alleging it received stolen goods. (Govan) We asked AFGRI SA for an interview. They declined but sent a statement saying there was no evidence for Ben’s claims. (Govan) Frustrated, Ben set up a sting operation to catch Masina red-handed. And he agreed to let us tag along. (Khensani Masina (Subtitles) Okay, where is that place so that I can come there? (Driver (Subtitles) I must know the price first. (Khensani Masina (Subtitles) White maize - I’m going to take it for R 60 000 (Driver (Subtitles) Okay, alright. (Govan) So the truck is in place and the security is armed this is a really important time - the truck is going to be parked on the N12 that's where the deal is happening but we can't be too close to them because it will tip off the syndicate - we're close enough to swoop on them once they arrive and inspect the maize (Govan) We wait for three hours and then… (Driver (Subtitles): Hello (Upsound Khensani Masina (Subtitles) Yes,I’m on my way. (Driver (Subtitles) : Alright. Okay. (Govan) And now it's just about getting there in time to stop her. (Govan) Here they are. looks like there - she's running she's running into the veld! They're giving chase! Oh there she is! (Govan) Security soon catches up, though, and we get a chance to ask Masina some questions. (Govan) How long have you been selling grain? (Govan) She pretends to be completely clueless about why we are here. (Govan) We know who you are. (Khensani Masina) Who am I? (Govan) You're trying to buy grain that you thought was stolen (Khensani Masina) No, I am not trying to buy anything. I was not trying to buy anything from anyone. (Govan) You are Khensani Masina ? (Khensani Masina) Yes I am Khensani (Khensani Masina) I do have documents, can I show you my documents? (Govan) Masina claims she leases a farm but doesn’t show us proof. (Govan) Do you have a folio number at AFGRI SA? (Khensani Masina) Yes, I do (Govan) But her story about why she’s here gets a little confusing. (Khensani Masina) This guy just called me and told me that he wants to see me (Govan) No, he wanted to sell stolen grain (Khensani Masina) NO, I didn't… (Govan) And you said yes. (Govan) We've got you recorded (Khensani Masina) Yes, it’s fine (Govan) We've got you recorded (Khensani Masina) Recorded with what? (Govan) Can you tell me why do you buy stolen grain (Khensani Masina) If people call me they'll say come I have this ..I'm coming. (Govan) So you don't check where the grain comes from? (Khensani Masina) I do check. (Govan) Are you running a grain theft syndicate Khensani? (Khensani Masina) No sir,no. (Govan) How long have you been selling grain to AFGRI SA? (Khensani Masina) I've been selling grain I think for almost 4 years now. (Govan) In other words, for the past 4 years Masina has probably been selling stolen grain to AFGRI SA. (Govan) We asked for confirmation on whether Masina has a folio account. AFGRI SA declined, citing confidentiality laws (Govan) AFGRI SA denied that it knowingly deals in stolen grain, or allocates accounts to criminals. (Govan) But it did admit that it only began to conduct site visits to confirm that its clients are in fact farmers, in October last year. (Khensani Masina) I don't know who are these guys and he's saying that this guy...yes. (Govan) My name is Govan Whittles from Carte Blanche. This is a sting operation and you've just been caught. (Khensani Masina) But I don't know the guy he just called me to come and see him. (Govan) We've recorded all your communication with him. You're in a lot of trouble. (Govan) The police are here and Ben's going to show them the warrant of arrest...Nkensani is smiling...she's clearly not afraid of them. (Govan) What she is worried about is the phone she says she lost in the maize field. (Govan) You're looking for a tilili... (Khensani Masina) Yes, tilili. (Govan) You know those phones are notorious for being used in crime, isn't that right officer? (Govan) I don't know if you believe in irony? (Khensani Masina) What is irony? (Govan) It's ironic that you're being arrested for grain theft and you're walking through a mealie field. (Khensani Masina) I do have the mealie field also. (Govan) Here's your smaller phone. You must be so relieved! (Govan) Ben, is this the woman that you suspect of stealing the load that you were transporting? (Ben Wepener) That is 100% her. She confirmed here on the site that she does have a folio number with AFGRI. (Govan) With Masina finally in custody and on her way to police cells, the truck driver covers the load up for safe delivery to its rightful owner. (Govan) On Ben’s information, two alleged members of the syndicate have now been arrested. He’s back on the hunt for two more.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Carte Blanche hunts down a logistics syndicate threatening the country's food security by the grain load.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Carte Blanche hunts down a logistics syndicate threatening the country's food security by the grain load. - Intercepting a compromised grain load before it's handed over to a criminal syndicate - Selling a sacrifical load to a legitimate grain leader: no questions asked - Confronting criminals as they alter horses and trailers at shady yards - Following the trail of a syndicate's grain hit
metadata.Summary: The clock is ticking for the agricultural industry - criminals are engaged in a dirty game forcing farmers and transporters to play but there are no rules. For years, the logistics industry had been under siege, no commodity is off limits for these greedy syndicates determined to profit off legitimate businesses sweat. Ben Wepener is a transporter and a former cop based in Delmas. In the dead of a night in June 2023, he received a call - his truck stood stationary kilometers from the silo where a client's grain was supposed to be loaded AND, his Zimbabwean driver was nowhere to be found. This set the wheels in motion for a one man investigation conducted by Ben. The goal: to track down his client's missing load. Through his determined sleuthing, he tracked the grain to AFGRI's silos. AFGRI is one of the leaders in the grain and production cycle. How did his client's legitimate load, "hijacked" by a criminal syndicate end up in AFGRI's legitimate silos?
metadata.Further information: How do we start the story:- Option 1: Ben on the stretch of road in Delmas Ben: This is where I found my truck, with no grain - completely empty and abandoned" Presenter: Where was the driver? Ben: I have no idea just like the grain he was nowhere to be found. Presenter: What did you do? Ben: I didnt waste time, I started investigating VO: And what he discovered will blow your mind. FADE TO BLACK Option 2: Open with track team chasing a truck or with presenter confronting criminals altering a horse at a trailer yard VO: You're about to join us on a ride through the murky underworld of dirty logistics. Elements Explored: AFGRI I am in the process of securing a Folio number from AFGRI which will permit us to sell a load at a SILO. I will record all interactions with the buyer. The purpose is to demonstrate the ease with which grain can be sold to AFGRI with few questions asked. Clearly, I have no agricultural background - where did I get the grain? Transporter, Ben Wepener has made arrangements with a farmer to provide a sacrificial load which we can sell to AFGRI. We will place GoPro’s on the truck as it makes its journey and a hidden camera on the driver to record interactions once he arrives at the depot. The cameraman will follow at a safe distance in order to secure a wide angle. The process of selling grain to AFGRI will be recorded so we will be clear on the checks and balances they have in place for interview. Note: consult legal on the receipt of funds into my bank account from AFGRI. Hijack or Handover Within the scope of their operations they say 90% of so-called hijackings are pre-arranged handovers between the syndicate and the truck drivers. They say almost all the drivers implicated are Zimbabwean in for a quick buck to send home and able to disappear because often they are not legally in the country. The team intercepted a truck “hijack”a few weeks ago and seized the drivers property including a phone. They have endless voicenotes and messages intricately planning the handover of the truck and the load. How we can use this: As part of the interview with Chris, he can allude to this incident and playback a few seconds of key moments of the planning between the driver and the syndicate to highlight the fact that the transport industry is at the mercy of these drivers - especially if they do not conduct proper checks. Intercepted Truck Takedown The source says hundreds of “hijackings” place on a daily basis. In fact, as I was sitting with them, they showed me a truck they were tracking on their phones. The calls come in unexpectedly as they don’t always have informers who know when robberies are planned. They’ve asked the team to be ready to receive a call at any time - even 2 a.m - which is quite challenging from a coordination perspective. Especially since the camera crew and the presenter would have to be on standby. This requires some planning. Cloning of trucks The syndicate secures transporters trailer registration numbers and clones them to avoid traceability. They showed me an image of a client’s trailer and the syndicate's cloned trailer with the client’s number plates. To legitimize their clandestine operations, the syndicate uses the cloned trucks to offload grain at the silos. Not only do they clone truck registrations, they hijack horse and trailers which they completely alter at shady trailer yards well-known to the team. Although they can alter license plates, the VIN number is often what the team uses to establish the vehicle has been cloned or stolen and altered. By altered, they spray paint, weld and use blowtorches in order to make the stolen vehicle almost untraceable. These vehicles are then taken crossborder where there’s allegedly great demand. How we can use this visually: The team will arrange a stakeout of a trailer yard and see what we can film from a distance. After 1 or 2 days of surveillance there will be a takedown. They asked if we have bulletproof vests - I said no and indicated we don't want to be in the middle of a shootout. They rather wear GoPros in case such an action movie takes place. We will move in once things have cooled down.
